Build a heterogeneous transition network

Source: R/build_htna.R
build_htna.Rd

build_htna() builds a heterogeneous transition network: one transition network over interaction sequences in which the events are produced by two or more types of actor, such as a learner and an AI assistant. In heterogeneous transition network analysis (HTNA) each node is a code (an action or event) and belongs to exactly one actor type, and each directed edge is the transition from one code to the next within a session (Lopez-Pernas, Misiejuk and Saqr, 2026). Because the actor partition is kept on the network, the within-actor transitions (Human to Human) and the hand-overs between actors (Human to AI, AI to Human) can be estimated, plotted and tested as distinct parts of one model.

build_htna() orders the events of every session in time, estimates the transition network over the combined sequence with the chosen method (relative transition probabilities by default, or frequencies, co-occurrences or attention weights), and attaches the actor type of every node. The actor partition can be given in three ways: a named list of one long data frame per actor type, a single data frame with a column naming the actor type of each row (actor_type), or a single data frame together with a code-to-actor lookup (node_groups). With group, one network is estimated per level of a session-level variable (for example an early and a late phase), in the order of the factor levels. A fitted sequence clustering (from Nestimate::build_clusters(), Nestimate::cluster_mmm() or tna::cluster_sequences()) is turned into one network per cluster without refitting, and a fitted Nestimate::build_mcml() model into one network whose actor types are its node clusters.

It returns an htna network, or an htna_group with one network per cohort or cluster. The grouped result is passed as it is to the comparison, assessment and plotting functions, which work through every cohort. Use summary.htna() to describe the result and as.data.frame.htna() for its edges and nodes.

Usage

build_htna(
  data,
  actor_type = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  node_groups = NULL,
  action = "code",
  session = "session_id",
  order = "order_in_session",
  method = "relative",
  group = NULL,
  disambiguate = FALSE,
  source_data = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The event data, in one of these forms:

  • a named list of long data frames, one per actor type, with the same columns, e.g. list(Human = human_simplified, AI = ai_simplified);

  • one long data frame, with actor_type or node_groups;

  • a fitted clustering (net_clustering, net_mmm, tna_clustering) or a netobject_group, giving one network per cluster;

  • a fitted mcml model, whose node clusters become the actor types.

actor_type

Name of the column giving the actor type of each row, for a single data frame. A factor column sets the order of the actor types; otherwise they are ordered by first appearance.

actor

Name of an optional column identifying the individual who produced each event (for example a learner id). Independent of actor_type. Default NULL.

node_groups

Code-to-actor lookup for a single data frame without an actor-type column: a named list of code vectors, e.g. list(Human = c("Specify", "Check"), AI = c("Plan", "Execute")), or a two-column data frame with the code column (named as action) and the actor-type column, such as human_ai_codebook. Every code must belong to exactly one actor type. For a clustering or mcml input it optionally supplies or overrides the partition. Use either actor_type or node_groups, not both.

action

Name of the code column. Default "code".

session

Name of the session column. Default "session_id".

order

Name of the within-session order column. Default "order_in_session".

method

Network estimator: "relative" (default, transition probabilities), "frequency", "co_occurrence" (undirected) or "attention".

group

Name of a session-level column defining cohorts; one network is built per cohort. Default NULL (one network).

disambiguate

If TRUE, a code used by more than one actor type is split into one node per actor type, prefixed with the actor label ("Human:Ask", "AI:Ask"). Default FALSE (a shared code is an error).

source_data

The original event data for an mcml input whose fitted object did not keep it. Default NULL.

...

Further estimation arguments, such as threshold or scaling.

Value

An object of class c("htna", "netobject", "cograph_network"): a transition network with its weight matrix, nodes, sequence data and the actor partition (the actor type of every node and the ordered actor types). With group or a clustering input, an htna_group: a named list with one htna network per cohort or cluster, which keeps the clustering assignments and diagnostics as attributes. An mcml input returns one htna. as.data.frame.htna() returns the edges (one row per non-zero transition, with the actor types of its source and target) or the nodes.

Conditions

Errors inherit from htna_error. Specific classes: htna_missing_column when the session, order or code column is absent; htna_actor_conflict when a code belongs to more than one actor type and disambiguate = FALSE; htna_unassigned_node when a code has no actor type in node_groups; htna_bad_input for other invalid arguments.

References

Lopez-Pernas, S., Misiejuk, K., & Saqr, M. (2026). How AI-generated feedback hinders or helps learning: A heterogeneous TNA study of learning dynamics. Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 42(4), e70285. doi:10.1002/jcal.70285

See also

summary.htna() and as.data.frame.htna() to describe the network; plot_htna() to draw it; compare_htna(), permutation_htna() and bootstrap_htna() for inference.

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
net
